transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, um, what brought me in is that I keep leaving my station at work. Like, I'll just pop up during meetings when I'm supposed to stay put, and my supervisor says it's becoming a safety problem because I just take off before I even think about it. Speaking of my supervisor, she has this really annoying habit of clicking her pen during those meetings. It’s like, click, click, click, the whole time. I don't know how anyone else focuses with that going on. Anyway, I think she got that pen from a conference in Vegas. I went to Vegas once, but it was so hot I barely left the hotel. They had this amazing buffet though... oh, wait, what was I saying? Right, the safety problem. Yeah, I just can't seem to stay in my seat.
Did you have similar trouble sitting still or staying focused back when you were a child?

Oh, definitely. Even in elementary school, I was the kid who just couldn't stay in my seat to save my life. I was always wandering around the room, looking at whatever. I remember my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she had this huge glass tank with a bearded dragon in it. His name was Spike, I think? I used to just get up and go stare at him right in the middle of math. She was always sending notes home to my mom because I kept blurting things out and talking right over her. My mom used to get so mad about those notes. She’d stick them on the fridge with these little magnet clips. We had this one magnet that looked like a slice of pizza, and it actually smelled like pizza for like, years. I always wondered what kind of chemicals they use to make plastic smell like pepperoni. It's probably toxic, honestly, especially in a factory. I work around some weird smelling stuff on the production line now, actually. But yeah, what were we talking about? Oh, right, being a kid. Yeah, I was always getting notes sent home for wandering off and talking.
Do you often find yourself making careless mistakes or having trouble organizing your daily tasks and activities?

Not really, no. I mean, my job on the line is pretty straightforward, so there isn't really much for me to organize, you know? I just stand at my station and pop these little rubber seals onto the metal caps as they come down the belt. It's super repetitive. The seals come in these huge bins, and sometimes they get all stuck together if it's too humid in the plant. The AC actually broke last month and it was just miserable in there. We had to keep the big loading dock doors wide open to get any air, and this stray cat kept wandering inside. We named him Barnaby. He was this big orange tabby, missing half an ear. I tried to give him some of my turkey sandwich on my break, but he just sniffed it and walked away. Cats are so weirdly picky, right? My aunt had a cat that would only eat if you put the food on a special ceramic plate. She lived down in Florida, though, so I guess she could afford to spoil it... wait, what did you ask me? Something about making mistakes? Yeah, no, I don't really have a problem with that.
Do you often feel restless inside, like you are constantly on the go or driven by a motor?

Yeah, all the time. It's like... if I try to just stand still by the machine, or if they make us sit through those long safety training videos, it feels like this intense pressure just starts building up inside my body. Like I physically have to move, or pace, or stretch, or just go do something right that second. Speaking of those training videos, they are so outdated. The actors in them have these huge cell phones and hairstyles from like the 90s. One of the guys in the forklift safety video looks exactly like my uncle Rick. Uncle Rick actually used to drive a forklift at a lumber yard before he hurt his back. He slipped on some ice in his driveway, not even at work. It was a whole big mess with his insurance. He had to wear this huge brace for like six months and he couldn't even drive his truck. He loved that truck, too. It was this bright cherry red Chevy. I've always wanted a red car, but my insurance would probably be so high. Red cars get pulled over more, right? Or is that just a myth? I read somewhere that silver is actually the most common car color. Anyway... what was the question? Oh, right, the restless thing. Yeah, I just can't stand still, it drives me crazy.
Do you ever have periods where you need much less sleep than usual, like only two or three hours, and still feel completely energized?

No, I definitely need my sleep. If I don't get at least like six or seven hours, I'm a total zombie on the line. I actually just got a new mattress, too, because my old one had this huge dip right in the middle. It was one of those memory foam ones that comes rolled up in a cardboard box? It's so crazy how they vacuum seal those things. When you cut the plastic, it just goes *whoosh* and inflates all at once. My friend Sarah helped me unbox it in my apartment, and she almost got smacked in the face when it popped open. 

Sarah's always getting into weird accidents like that, honestly. Last year she tripped over her own dog and sprained her wrist right before we were supposed to go to this concert. It was an outdoor country music thing, which I don't even really like country that much, but the tickets were free. I think a local radio station was giving them away. They do those call-in contests, you know? Like, be the ninth caller to win. I tried to win tickets to a comedy show once and dialed the number like fifty times, but all I got was a busy signal. Do people even use landlines anymore to get busy signals? My grandma still has one. It's an actual rotary dial phone, which takes forever to use if there's a lot of nines in the number. 

Wait... what were we talking about? Oh, sleep. Right. Yeah, no, I don't ever feel energized on just two hours. I'd be completely dead.
Do you often lose or misplace things that you need for everyday tasks, like your keys, wallet, or phone?

No, I don't really lose stuff like that. I mean, I keep my keys on this big lanyard, so it's pretty hard to miss. It's got all these little enamel pins on it that I've collected. One of them is a tiny slice of pizza with sunglasses on. I got it at this weird little thrift shop downtown. That place is amazing, they have all these old denim jackets from the 80s and bins full of vintage records. I don't even own a record player, but I almost bought this one album just because the cover art was so cool. It was like this neon laser grid with a panther jumping through it. 

Panthers are such beautiful animals, don't you think? I watched this documentary on them a while back. Or maybe it was jaguars? Whichever one lives in the jungle. They were talking about how their spots are like fingerprints, no two are exactly the same. Kind of like snowflakes. I haven't seen real snow in years. We got that one flurry last winter, but it melted as soon as it hit the pavement. It was so disappointing. People still rushed to the grocery store and bought all the bread and milk, though. I never understood that. Like, if the power goes out, the milk is just going to go bad anyway, right? You should buy stuff in cans. Soup, or like, Spaghettios. I used to eat Spaghettios all the time when I was a kid. 

Anyway... wait, what did you ask me? Losing things? Yeah, no, I usually know where my phone and stuff are.
